nodes.description: Destruction of infected erythrocytes produces hemolysis, anemia, bilirubin generation, and downstream systemic manifestations. Babesiosis reaches the conserved premature-erythrocyte-destruction step by an infectious route: intraerythrocytic parasite replication lyses the host cell directly, and splenic macrophages additionally remove parasitized red cells. The destruction step, not the upstream cause, is what this entry shares with the hereditary and autoimmune hemolytic anemias.

nodes.description: Asplenia, advanced age, and immunosuppressive disease or therapy impair parasite clearance, enabling persistent or relapsing infection and raising the risk of high parasite burden. The specific risk set is informative about which defenses matter: asplenia removes the filtration site for parasitized erythrocytes, while B-cell lymphoma and rituximab — singled out by CDC — implicate humoral immunity alongside the CD4/IFN-gamma cellular arm demonstrated in mouse models. Congestive heart failure appears on the severe-disease risk list as a host vulnerability, not as a manifestation.
